audit_notes: Model: steady 1D conduction through the wall; the outer wall surface behind a ventilated screen receives the transmitted sun, convection to cavity air at ambient temperature and linearised longwave exchange with the screen, whose temperature follows from its own two-sided balance T_f = T_a + (alpha_f*I - eps_f*R_net)/(2*h_f) (screen back-face exchange with the wall neglected in the screen balance, a small error). Adjustments: screen absorptance 0.07 is a clean-fabric value; over 20 years dust on a woven fabric raises it; I use a life-mean 0.10. Transmittance 0.10 is consistent with a dense scattering weave. Baseline (bare painted wall) is represented in the same equation by tau = 1, alpha_f = 0 (no screen), cavity coefficient 10 plus radiative 5 = 15 W/m2K outer film, and screen_convection_coefficient = 2.5 so that the radiative term becomes the wall's own sky loss eps_w*R_net = 36 W/m2; this reproduces the direct sol-air result 5.59 W/m2. Hand result: design T_f - T_a = (18 - 36)/20 = -0.9 K; wall gradient = (0.33*0.1*180 + 5*10 + 5*9.1)/10.5 = 9.66 K -> q = 4.83 W/m2 vs 5.59 W/m2: -14 %. Peak hour (I=700, T_a=43 C): ~-35 %. A conventional PTFE-coated glass fabric (alpha 0.15, tau 0.12) gives ~5.0 W/m2 (-11 %), so the voided fibre adds only ~3 points. Dimensionless: screen Biot-type ratio h_r/(h_c + h_r) = 0.5. Structural: glass-fibre fabrics in tension carry wind loads (tensile strength ~3-4 kN/5 cm), UV-stable; risks are fibre fatigue at clamps under flutter, and the unproven drawing of voided fibres. Simulation coefficient: total wall-side conductance h_c + h_r = 10 W/m2K.
